questions.scenario: Company policy requires that the temporary disk and the OS and data disk caches of VM1 are encrypted. VM1 uses managed disks with server-side encryption and platform-managed keys.
questions.question: What should you enable?

options.why: Correct. Encryption at host encrypts the temporary disk and disk caches on the host.

options.text: Customer-managed keys by using a disk encryption set
options.why: This changes the key used for managed disks at rest but does not cover the temporary disk or caches.
This applies to storage accounts, not VM temporary disks.
Trusted launch adds Secure Boot and vTPM. It does not encrypt the temporary disk.

questions.explanation: Server-side encryption covers managed disks at rest. Encryption at host extends encryption to the temp disk and caches.

questions.scenario: You plan to enable encryption at host on an existing running virtual machine named VM1. The feature has never been used in the subscription.
questions.question: Which two actions must you perform before you can enable encryption at host on VM1? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Register the EncryptionAtHost feature for the Microsoft.Compute namespace
options.why: Correct. The feature must be registered for the subscription.
Correct. Encryption at host can be changed only while the VM is deallocated.

options.text: Enable Azure Disk Encryption on VM1
options.why: Azure Disk Encryption cannot be combined with encryption at host on the same VM.

options.text: Convert all disks to Standard HDD
options.why: Disk type changes are not required.
A vault is used for backup and is not required.

questions.explanation: Register the feature, then deallocate the VM, set securityProfile.encryptionAtHost to true, and start the VM.

questions.scenario: VM1 is running and has a 128 GiB Premium SSD data disk named Disk1. You need to change Disk1 to Standard SSD.
questions.question: What should you do first?

options.why: Correct. The disk type of an attached disk can be changed only when the VM is deallocated or the disk is detached.
A snapshot is a good precaution but is not required to change the type.
Managed disks cannot be shrunk.
Host caching does not affect the ability to change the disk type.

questions.explanation: After the change, start the VM or reattach the disk. Disk sizes can only be increased.

questions.question: A VM was deallocated and then started. Files that an application saved to drive D: are missing, but files on drive C: and on a data disk mounted as F: are intact. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Drive D: is the temporary disk, which does not persist when the VM moves to another host
options.why: Correct. The temporary disk is local to the host and its data can be lost after deallocation.

options.text: Drive D: was encrypted by using encryption at host
options.why: Encryption does not delete data.
The data disk F: is intact.
Drive C: is intact.

questions.explanation: Use the temporary disk only for page files, swap, and scratch data.

questions.question: You need to add a new 256 GiB Premium SSD data disk to a running Linux VM named VM1 without restarting it. Which command should you run?

options.text: az vm disk attach --resource-group RG1 --vm-name VM1 --name Data1 --new --size-gb 256 --sku Premium_LRS
options.why: Correct. Data disks can be created and attached to a running VM.
This resizes an existing disk named VM1 and does not attach a new disk.

options.text: az vm resize --resource-group RG1 --name VM1 --size Standard_D4s_v5
options.why: Resizing changes the VM size and restarts the VM.

options.text: az vm update --resource-group RG1 --name VM1 --set securityProfile.encryptionAtHost=true
options.why: This configures encryption at host and requires the VM to be deallocated.

questions.explanation: After attaching, partition, format, and mount the disk inside the operating system.
